chunks.arabic_text: رَوَى الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ خَالِدٍ عَنْ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الْأَوَّلِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ

translations.en: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Khālid narrated from Abī al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام

chunks.arabic_text: أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَتَى رَجُلًا وَهُوَ رَاقِدٌ فَلَمَّا صَارَ عَلَى ظَهْرِهِ انْتَبَهَ فَبَعَجَهُ بَعْجَةً فَقَتَلَهُ

translations.en: that he was asked about a man who came upon another man while he was lying down. Then when he got onto his back, he awoke and struck him with a forceful blow, killing him.

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ لَا دِيَةَ لَهُ وَلَا قَوَدَ

translations.en: He عليه السلام said: "There is no diyah for him, nor is there qawad."

en.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a man who approaches a sleeping person and is then killed when the sleeper wakes and violently repels him. The Imam عليه السلام rules that in such a case there is neither diyah nor legal retaliation for the one who was killed, indicating no liability upon the one who defended himself.
en.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone is killed after attacking or violating a sleeping person?

key_terms.بَعْجَةً: a forceful strike or violent blow
key_terms.دِيَةَ: blood money or financial compensation for killing
